title: Add RAG chaos-prober mini-lab and tool-resilience playbook
author: Evan Liu
release_notes: Adds a new developer-facing quickstart: a compact RAG mini-lab that demonstrates tool failure injection, chaos probing of tool timeouts, and telemetry-driven rollback policies. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see customers struggle to understand how tool-calling chains behave under partial failure and intermittent latency (ENG-1284). This quickstart provides a small, local-first lab that developers can run in minutes to exercise tool-resilience patterns: timeouts, retries, fallback tools, and telemetry-driven canaries. It complements existing RAG authoring guides by focusing on reliability and SLO-aware tooling rather than ingest/index patterns.

What this PR adds: a compact 'mini-lab' under quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober with: 1) a runnable Node + Python microservice pair that simulate tool latency/failure modes, 2) an instrumented RAG agent sample showing debounce/retry/backoff strategies, 3) a telemetry probe harness (Prometheus + lightweight export) and an authoring checklist for evaluating failure modes locally, 4) CI smoke tests and a small e2e runner for the devcontainer.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add quickstart content and README with step-by-step lab instructions and learning objectives
- [x] Provide sample tool adapters with deterministic failure injection flags
- [x] Add telemetry probes and live dashboard examples (Grafana JSON)
- [x] CI smoke test for local run in devcontainer (lightweight)
- [x] Docs blurb for docs.redwood.ai referencing the new lab

Commits (summary):
- 19f7c2e: initial quickstart skeleton and README with learning objectives
- 5a1d3b9: add chaos-prober microservice and failure flags, sample tool adapters
- c4e2b11: instrumentation: Prometheus metrics + example Grafana panel; add smoke e2e runner
- d3b7f8a: fix CI matrix and documentation copy tweaks; address review comments

Files changed (high-level):
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/README.md - new, developer-facing lab guide with step-by-step run, expected outputs, and validation checklist
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/devcontainer.json - devcontainer for local sandboxing
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/prober-service/main.py - Python microservice that simulates tool latency/failure (flags for p50/p95 error rates)
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/agent-samples/node-agent/index.ts - example RAG agent demonstrating tool-calling resilience patterns and structured fallbacks
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/telemetry/prometheus.yml and grafana/dashboard.json - probe examples for local dashboards
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/.github/workflows/mini-lab-smoke.yml - lightweight CI smoke runner to build devcontainer and run the demo (fast)
- quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober/tests/smoke_runner.sh - small e2e script used by CI

Review conversation (high level, single-threaded transcript):
Aisha Raman (reviewer): "Love the learning objectives. Can we make the failure flags deterministic so CI isn't flaky? Also suggest adding a short Troubleshooting section for common Windows devcontainer issues."
Evan Liu (author): "Agree — added deterministic seed option on the prober service and included a Troubleshooting appendix. CI now runs with seed=42 in the matrix."
Marco Delgado (reviewer): "Telemetry looks great. Suggest we reduce retention in prometheus.yml defaults so local runs don't keep large TSDB files. Also can we add a small note about sanitizing telemetry before sharing screenshots?"
Evan Liu (author): "Reduced retention to 1h for local runs and added a callout about data sanitization. Thanks."
Priya Nair (approver): "Approving after minor doc wording nit; please squash the fixup commits."

CI checks: 
- actions/mini-lab-smoke (ubuntu-latest) - passed (rerun after deterministic seed change)
- lint/markdown - passed
- tests/smoke - passed (containerized smoke runner completed in ~45s)
- security/scan - informational (no high severity findings)

Notes on flakiness and mitigation: Initial run had a transient failure in tests/smoke due to non-deterministic prober behavior (random seeds). I updated the prober to accept --seed and made the CI invocation pass --seed=42. Added a short unit test that asserts the prober respects the seed to prevent regressions.

Documentation and linking: Added a short blurb under docs/quickstarts/index.md referencing the mini-lab and added a cross-link from the RAG reliability section. Also created a small entry for the docs site team to surface this lab under "resilience and canaries". Linear tickets ENG-1284 and ENG-1307 are linked in the PR body for context.

Merge: Squash-merged once reviewers approved. Post-merge tasks: create a docs.redwood.ai PR to import the README as a quickstart page (assigned to Docs team), and pin the quickstart to the next "learning-lab" newsletter.

How to run locally (short): 
1) git clone && cd quickstarts/rag-chaos-prober
2) ./devcontainer.sh (or run the devcontainer in VSCode)
3) make run-prober && make run-agent  # runs both prober and agent sample
4) open http://localhost:3000/dashboard (Grafana) to watch Prometheus metrics and exercise timeouts

Why this is different: Most quickstarts focus on authoring, indexing, or toolbinding. This lab is intentionally small and orthogonal — it is teaching resilience patterns with observable metrics and deterministic failure injection so developers can reproduce and iterate on robustness strategies quickly.

If anything unexpected comes up after merge, ping me (Evan) or Aisha on the Linear thread ENG-1284.
